prs.title: fix(client): replace PayPal Buttons.driver with react-paypal-js
prs.author_claim:
## Summary
PayPal's legacy `Buttons.driver('react', { React, ReactDOM })` adapter calls `ReactDOM.findDOMNode` in its own `componentDidMount`, which React 19 removed ÔÇö it threw during commit and, with no error boundary above it, unmounted the whole donate page rather than just the button. Replacing it with `@paypal/react-paypal-js`, which renders through a ref and ships its own error boundary, deletes `paypal-button-script-loader.tsx` outright and unblocks the React 19 upgrade (#69271, reverted in #69474). Verified locally against a real client id: `paypal-donation.spec.ts` passes 6/6 on both React 18 and React 19, where pre-migration React 19 gave a blank page and `TypeError: i.findDOMNode is not a function`.
### Test fake update
The fake SDK added in #69477 implements only what `Buttons.driver` needed. `@paypal/react-paypal-js` also calls `isEligible()` and chains `.catch()` onto `render()`, so both are added here, and the now-unused `Buttons.driver` branch is dropped so the fake matches how the SDK is actually consumed.

subagent_a.true_summary: The diff migrates the PayPal donation button from a custom class-component adapter that used the legacy window.paypal.Buttons.driver('react', {React, ReactDOM}) API with manual script tag injection/removal, to the official @paypal/react-paypal-js library. The deleted paypal-button-script-loader.tsx (204-line class component) is replaced by a function component in paypal-button.tsx that wraps <PayPalScriptProvider> and <PayPalButtons> from the new package. Script lifecycle management moves from imperative componentDidUpdate DOM manipulation to a useEffect hook dispatching DISPATCH_ACTION.RESET_OPTIONS. The createOrder call gains an explicit intent:'CAPTURE' field not present in the old code, onApprove is refactored from .then() chaining to async/await (with optional chaining on actions.order?.capture()), a hardcoded alwaysDisabledFunding list of 11 payment methods is introduced, the isPaypalLoading/isSubscription/ref props are removed from the public interface, and the e2e mock is updated to drop Buttons.driver() and add isEligible() and a resolved render() promise.
undisclosed_changes: A hardcoded alwaysDisabledFunding array permanently disables 11 funding sources (credit, bancontact, blik, eps, giropay, ideal, mybank, p24, sepa, sofort, venmo) with no configuration path to re-enable them.
createOrder now sends intent:'CAPTURE' explicitly to the PayPal API; the old code omitted this field, making this a behavioral change to the payment flow not mentioned in the description.
onApprove switches to async/await with actions.order?.capture() using optional chaining — if actions.order is undefined, the capture is silently skipped with no error surfaced.
The isPaypalLoading prop and its loading-state pass-through from donate-form.tsx are silently removed, potentially breaking loading UX for donors while the SDK initializes.
The isSubscription prop is removed from PaypalButton's public interface with no documented migration path.
The ref? prop is removed from PaypalButton, breaking any parent that held a ref to the class component instance.
Six new transitive runtime dependencies are added (including server-only@0.0.1 and promise-polyfill@8.3.0) — none mentioned in the description beyond the top-level package.

scope_flags.detail: createOrder adds intent:'CAPTURE' — a behavioral change to the PayPal order intent not justified or mentioned by the adapter-swap rationale.
onApprove is changed to async and now awaits a capture call, introducing new server-round-trip logic not described anywhere in the PR description.
New alwaysDisabledFunding constant and getScriptOptions helper are added — neither mentioned or justified in the description.
Removal of isSubscription prop from paypal-button.tsx changes the component's public interface beyond what is needed to swap the underlying adapter.
server-only@0.0.1 appears as a new transitive dependency for a client-side package, which may affect build target assumptions.
The description claims the new library 'ships its own error boundary' but no error boundary wiring or test is visible in the diff.
The description says the fix 'unblocks the React 19 upgrade' but no React version bump or revert of #69474 is present, leaving the stated goal only partially achieved.

predicted_questions.question: The onApprove handler for one-time payments calls onApprove(details) after actions.order?.capture(), but the TODO comment admits 'passing details looks wrong but the api ignores it for now'. What does the upstream callback actually expect, and is there a risk a future API change silently breaks payment confirmation?

createOrder now hardcodes intent:'CAPTURE' — was this intent previously configured elsewhere, and could adding it here conflict with subscription flows where the intent should be SUBSCRIPTION rather than CAPTURE?

The useEffect dispatching DISPATCH_ACTION.RESET_OPTIONS is gated on optionsKey changing — could it trigger an extra SDK reload on initial mount, causing a missed handlePaymentButtonLoad call if isResolved fires before the reset completes?

The isPaypalLoading prop and loading.paypal state are removed from donate-form.tsx. What now controls the loading/disabled UX while the PayPal SDK initialises, and is there a window where the button appears interactive before the SDK is ready?

The e2e fake SDK drops the Buttons.driver stub entirely and only mocks at the window.paypal.Buttons level. Do the e2e tests now actually exercise the PayPalButtons React component code path, or are they too shallow to catch regressions in onApprove and createOrder?

server-only@0.0.1 and promise-polyfill@8.3.0 are new transitive dependencies pulled in by @paypal/react-paypal-js — has there been any vetting that server-only does not cause issues if accidentally imported into the client-side bundle?

prs.disagreement_note: The Scope Auditor rated intent:'CAPTURE' and async onApprove as medium-severity scope flags (undisclosed additions), while both the Technical Truth-Teller and Reviewer's Ghost independently rated these same payment-flow changes as high-risk due to the potential for silent capture failures and incorrect payload forwarding to the donation backend.

prs.title: feat(client): upgrade to React 19
prs.author_claim:
## Summary
- Upgrades `react`, `react-dom`, `@types/react`, `@types/react-dom`, and `@testing-library/react` from 18 to 19, and drops the now-unused `react-test-renderer`/`@types/react-test-renderer`.
- Updates icon component type signatures to match React 19's JSX types.
- Fixes a `react-helmet` + Gatsby incompatibility under React 19: Gatsby 5.16.1 monkey-patches `React.createElement` for `title`/`meta`/`link` elements to support its own Head API. This changes `child.type` away from the plain string `'title'`, so `react-helmet` can no longer recognize a `<title>` child element and silently drops it, leaving `document.title` empty on the client for every page that rendered its title as `<title>{title}</title>` JSX. Fixed by passing the title through Helmet's `title` prop instead, which avoids creating a `<title>` element via JSX and sidesteps the patch. Verified against a real production build with Playwright, not just unit tests.

subagent_a.true_summary: Upgrades React and related packages from v18 to v19 in `client/package.json`: `react` and `react-dom` from 18.3.1 to 19.2.8, `@types/react` from 18.3.28 to 19.2.17, `@types/react-dom` from 18.3.7 to 19.2.3, `@testing-library/react` from 14.3.1 to 16.3.2. Drops `react-test-renderer` and `@types/react-test-renderer` (both removed). Fixes a `react-helmet` + Gatsby SSR incompatibility by adding `void` before `headComponents.sort(...)` in `gatsby-ssr.tsx` (suppresses the unused return value). Updates icon component type signatures across ~80 `.tsx` files in `client/src/assets/icons/` by removing `JSX.IntrinsicAttributes &` from prop types (React 19 dropped the `JSX.IntrinsicAttributes` requirement). Adds `pnpm-lock.yaml` updates for all new package versions.
undisclosed_changes: The PR description mentions upgrading React 18 → 19, dropping react-test-renderer, and fixing icon type signatures. It does not explicitly describe the `gatsby-ssr.tsx` change (`void headComponents.sort(...)`) — this is a targeted workaround for a react-helmet/Gatsby incompatibility and deserves its own explanation since it silences a lint warning rather than fixing the root cause.

The `void headComponents.sort(...)` change in `gatsby-ssr.tsx` is the exact inverse of what PR #69474 (a revert) will later undo — meaning this change was shipped, then a problem emerged, and it was reverted. The description does not flag that this is a known-fragile workaround.
The description does not mention that removing `JSX.IntrinsicAttributes &` from ~80 icon components could affect TypeScript consumers that relied on those attributes being required.
The lock file gains substantial new entries (React 19 transitive deps) not discussed in the description.

scope_flags.detail: Bulk type-signature changes to ~80 icon files is a large mechanical change not highlighted as a separate concern in the description — reviewers may not notice the semantic effect on TypeScript consumers.

predicted_questions.question: The `void headComponents.sort(...)` suppresses the ESLint 'no unused expression' warning but does not explain *why* the sort's return value needs to be suppressed. What exactly is the react-helmet + Gatsby conflict, and is `void` the correct fix or a temporary workaround?

Removing `react-test-renderer` and `@types/react-test-renderer` — were all usages audited to confirm nothing in the test suite still imports them? The lock file removal is shown but no test file changes appear in the diff.

The icon type change removes `JSX.IntrinsicAttributes &` from all props. In React 19, `JSX.IntrinsicAttributes` is now merged into the base component interface. Were there cases where having `IntrinsicAttributes` explicit was providing stricter type checking that is now lost?

prs.title: fix(client): correct RTL layout on settings, profile and superblock pages
prs.author_claim:
Fixes RTL layout on the settings, profile and superblock pages: the settings sidebar border and active-item highlight sat on the wrong edge and the page scrolled horizontally, the profile Edit/Add buttons and camper badge did not mirror, and the superblock rulers, dropdown icons, search icons and accordion tags were all on the wrong side.
Each one came from a physical CSS property that does not flip for RTL, so the fix throughout is the logical equivalent. LTR was measured alongside RTL on every change and is unchanged.
rel https://github.com/freeCodeCamp/freeCodeCamp/issues/67661

subagent_a.true_summary: This diff replaces physical CSS directional properties with their logical equivalents across seven client-side files to fix RTL (right-to-left) layout issues. In show-settings.css, padding-left is replaced with padding-inline-start in two rules, a shorthand padding is decomposed into padding-block and padding-inline, and a new [dir='rtl'] rule is added to flip the active-item box-shadow to the correct edge. In header.css, three instances of left on .skip-to-content-button are replaced with inset-inline-start. In camper.css, right is replaced with inset-inline-end, margin-left with margin-inline-start, and margin-right with margin-inline-end. In experience-display.tsx and portfolio-projects.tsx, inline React styles use marginInlineStart instead of marginLeft. In toggle-setting.css, left: -9999px becomes inset-inline-start: -9999px. In sidebar-panel.css, border-right becomes border-inline-end. In super-block-accordion.css, two padding-left: 0 rules become padding-inline-start: 0, two left positional values become inset-inline-start, a new .tags-wrapper rule sets padding-inline: 64px 10px (replacing an implicit left-only padding), and a new [dir='rtl'] block is added to apply transform: rotate(-90deg) on collapsed dropdown icons for chapter, module, and block headers. In super-block-search.css, left on the magnifier icon becomes inset-inline-start and right on the reset button becomes inset-inline-end.
undisclosed_changes: In show-settings.css, the shorthand `padding: 0 1rem 0rem 2rem` is decomposed into `padding-block: 0` and `padding-inline: 2rem 1rem`, which reverses the inline start/end values compared to the original (original had padding-left 2rem, padding-right 1rem; new has padding-inline-start 2rem, padding-inline-end 1rem) — the description does not call out this specific padding decomposition.

In super-block-accordion.css, a new `.super-block-accordion .module-panel .accordion-block-expanded .tags-wrapper { padding-inline: 64px 10px }` rule is added — this is a net-new rule with a specific hard-coded 64px value, not merely a logical replacement of an existing physical property, and is not explicitly mentioned in the PR description.

The [dir='rtl'] dropdown icon rotation rule in super-block-accordion.css uses rotate(-90deg) for the collapsed state, which is the mirror of the LTR rotate(90deg) — the description mentions fixing dropdown icons but does not describe this specific transform direction detail.

In toggle-setting.css, `left: -9999px` (used to visually hide a radio input off-screen) is changed to `inset-inline-start: -9999px` — the description does not mention this accessibility/visually-hidden pattern change.

predicted_questions.question: In show-settings.css (padding decomposition), the logical shorthand `padding-inline: 2rem 1rem` maps inline-start to 2rem and inline-end to 1rem — identical to the original LTR physical values. Was the start/end order intentionally preserved, or was the mapping accidentally swapped given that CSS logical shorthand is start-first?

In show-settings.css, an explicit `[dir='rtl']` rule is added to flip the box-shadow active-item highlight. Why was this done with a direction-specific selector rather than using a logical approach (e.g., border-inline-start) that would avoid needing a separate RTL override entirely?

In super-block-accordion.css, a `[dir='rtl']` rule is added to rotate .dropdown-icon to -90deg for collapsed buttons. Is there a corresponding [dir='rtl'] rule for the *expanded* state icon, or will expanded icons in RTL render incorrectly?

In super-block-accordion.css, a new rule targets `.tags-wrapper` with `padding-inline: 64px 10px`. This does not appear to be a 1:1 replacement of an existing physical property — what is the origin of the 64px value, and was an equivalent rule previously defined elsewhere that was missed?

The PR description states 'LTR was measured alongside RTL on every change and is unchanged.' Are there automated visual regression or RTL-specific integration tests covering these components, or is this assurance based solely on manual testing?

prs.title: fix(client): update JSON module imports
prs.author_claim:
## Problem
Webpack emits warnings when the client imports properties directly from JSON modules, for example:
```text
Should not import the named export 'apiLocation' (imported as 'apiLocation') from default-exporting module (only default export is available soon)
```
The same warning appears for client environment values such as `clientLocale`, `radioLocation`, and the Algolia configuration, as well as package `version` imports used by the challenge builder and browser worker tooling.
## Summary
This replaces named imports and re-exports from JSON modules with default imports followed by property access or destructuring.
It updates client environment configuration imports and package-version imports used by the challenge builder and browser worker tooling. This removes Webpack's deprecated named JSON export warnings without changing runtime behavior.
## Testing
- Client type-check and lint
- 32 focused client tests
- Challenge-builder type-check, lint, and build
- Browser-scripts lint and production Webpack build
- Focused TypeScript checks for the changed browser scripts

subagent_a.true_summary: Replaces named imports from JSON modules with default-import-then-destructure across 12 files in `client/src/` and 2 files in `client/tools/`, plus 2 files in `tools/client-plugins/` and 1 in `packages/challenge-builder/src/`. The pattern is consistent: `import { X } from 'module.json'` becomes `import envData from 'module.json'; const { X } = envData;` (for env.json imports) and `import { version } from 'package.json'` becomes `import pkg from 'package.json'; ... pkg.version` (for package.json version imports). One exception: `independent-lower-jaw.tsx` moves the destructuring inside the component function body rather than at module scope. The stated motivation is eliminating Webpack 'should not import named export' warnings from default-only JSON modules.
undisclosed_changes: In `independent-lower-jaw.tsx`, the destructuring `const { apiLocation, clientLocale } = envData;` is placed *inside* the component function body rather than at module scope (as done in all other files). This means it re-evaluates on every render. The description does not mention or justify this inconsistency.

The diff touches files outside `client/src/` — specifically `tools/client-plugins/browser-scripts/copy-scripts.ts`, `sass-compile.ts`, `test-runner.ts`, and `packages/challenge-builder/src/transformers.js`. The PR description says 'This replaces named imports... with default imports' but does not enumerate the non-client-src scope.

In `test-runner.ts`, `export { version } from '...'` is replaced with `export const version = curriculumHelpers.version;` — this changes from a re-export to a computed const export, which is a subtle semantic difference (the re-export was live binding; the const is a snapshot at module initialization time).

scope_flags.detail: Changes extend beyond client/src/ into tools/ and packages/ without the description calling this out.

predicted_questions.question: In `independent-lower-jaw.tsx`, why was `const { apiLocation, clientLocale } = envData;` placed inside the component function rather than at module scope like all other files in this PR? Is this intentional for any reason, or an oversight?

The `export { version }` re-export in `test-runner.ts` is changed to `export const version = curriculumHelpers.version;`. Are there downstream consumers that import `version` from this module and could be affected by the binding type changing from a live re-export to a snapshot const?
Do the Webpack warnings being fixed affect development builds, production builds, or both? Is there a CI step or log sample that shows the warnings are now gone?

prs.title: fix(client): drop the stray closing paren from formatted Map output
prs.author_claim:
### What
The Map branch of `format()` in `client/src/utils/format.js` closes its template literal with `}})` while the adjacent Set branch correctly closes with `}}`. Every Map printed in the challenge test-runner console panel (format is what `frame.ts` feeds the console) carries a stray trailing `)`:
```
format(new Map([['a', 1], ['b', 2]]))  ->  "Map(2) {a => 1, b => 2})"
format(new Map())                      ->  "Map(0) {})"
```
The file's own comment says it is "trying to mimic console.log", and Node prints `Map(2) { 'a' => 1, 'b' => 2 }` with no trailing paren.
### Changes
The stray `)` is removed in both copies of the file (`client/src/utils/format.js` and `tools/client-plugins/browser-scripts/utils/format.js`), and `formats Sets` / `formats Maps` cases are added to `client/src/utils/format.test.ts`, which previously covered neither branch.
### Verification
With the fix, the format suite passes 9/9. Reverting only the Map line while keeping the tests fails with `expected 'Map(0) {})' to be 'Map(0) {}'`; restoring passes again. Prettier reports no differences on the changed files.

subagent_a.true_summary: Fixes a stray trailing `)` in the Map branch of `format()` by changing `}})` to `}}` in the template literal closing. The fix is applied identically in two separate copies of the file: `client/src/utils/format.js` and `tools/client-plugins/browser-scripts/utils/format.js`. A new test file `client/src/utils/format.test.ts` gains 15 lines of tests covering Set and Map formatting (empty and non-empty cases). The PR description accurately labels these as '### What' (bug) and '### Why' (Maps in the test-runner console panel showed a stray `)`).
undisclosed_changes: The fix is applied to two copies of `format.js` (one under `client/src/utils/` and one under `tools/client-plugins/browser-scripts/utils/`), but the description only mentions `client/src/utils/format.js`. The duplication and its implications are not discussed.

The description does not mention that the existing `format.test.ts` file already existed and was extended; it frames the test additions as new, but does not clarify whether there were pre-existing tests for Map/Set.

prs.title: fix(client): preserve spaces in hint code
prs.author_claim:
Closes #67697
This preserve spaces in inline code blocks when they are displayed in the lower jaw

subagent_a.true_summary: Adds a single CSS rule to `client/src/templates/Challenges/components/independent-lower-jaw.css` that sets `white-space: pre-wrap; overflow-wrap: anywhere;` on `.independent-lower-jaw .hint-body code`. This preserves whitespace and wraps long code strings inside hint code blocks. Closes issue #67697, whose title identifies the real bug (spaces trimmed in IndependentLowerJaw hint code blocks) — matching this fix exactly. The linked ticket's body also separately mentions an unrelated pyramid test-case expected-output complaint, which this PR does not address; that is a distinct issue from the one named in the ticket's title and is not part of this PR's actual scope.

prs.author_claim: This fixes a bug noticed in https://www.freecodecamp.org/arabic/learn/a2-english-for-developers/learn-greetings-in-your-first-day-at-the-office/task-2, where spans with the target language to be taught get the final punctuation in the beginning of the span.
